30 Dec 2024ATLAS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

OmniFold enables an unbinned 24-dimensional Z+jets cross-section measurement by ATLAS

Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset. The measured total fiducial cross section is 1,808 ± 42 fb; most illustrative differential bins have 3–5% total uncertainty, rising to about 15% in tails. The measurement is more precise than the compared predictions for many distributions, especially Sherpa. The event-level release also supports derived observables, including an infrared-and-collinear-safe τ₂₁ measurement in a specified fiducial region.

Technology: OmniFold iterative machine-learning unfolding

Relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: direct test
  • Tested: Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset.
  • Still unknown: This is a new high-dimensional precision measurement of known Z+jets production, not a new particle or beyond-Standard-Model discovery. The released measurement is unbinned in 24 measured variables; displayed plots may be binned for presentation. The authors report mostly 3–5% uncertainties in illustrative bins, up to about 15% in tails, with dominant unfolding-prior/hidden-variable uncertainties for some observables. Pseudo-data closure is generally good, with exceptions including a p-value of 0.038 for leading-jet transverse momentum; users are given phase-space and covariance-use guidance.
  • AI role: OmniFold used neural-network classifiers to iteratively reweight simulated events so the detector-level simulation matched collision data, then propagated the learned correction to particle-level events. That multivariate unfolding handled 24 correlated observables simultaneously and produced event weights with uncertainty variations, enabling a high-dimensional unbinned measurement and event-level construction of additional derived observables. The paper validates closure on pseudo-data and reports its uncertainty components.

Evidence sources: https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.261803

30 Dec 2024Institute for Artificial Intelligence & Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

Machine-learning screening identifies two drug-repurposing candidates against tuberculosis

A virtual-screening workflow combined XGBoost and graph-neural-network models to screen 11,576 DrugBank compounds. Researchers selected 15 candidates for evaluation; four met the study’s activity cutoff against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv. Aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin were further tested against multidrug-resistant isolates, intracellular bacteria and recombinant DNA gyrase. These are laboratory repurposing results, not evidence of patient benefit or clinical safety. A same-team patent-family publication predates the journal article; this record makes no priority claim over patent disclosures. Concentration values are omitted because of inconsistent units in the rendered tables.

Technology: Ensemble virtual screening with XGBoost and graph neural networks

26 Dec 2024Shanghai Jiao Tong University

Protein language model guides creatinase stability optimization

A deep protein language model used prior single- and multiple-mutant measurements to guide combinations across two design/test rounds. The 13-substitution variant 13M4 reportedly retained nearly wild-type catalytic activity and increased apparent melting temperature by 10.19 °C. This assay does not establish long-term stability across production conditions, and the model recombined previously measured mutations.

17 Dec 2024Rutgers University; Flatiron Institute; University of South Carolina; Princeton University; Michigan State University

Machine-learning-guided synthesis confirms superconductivity in Mo20Re6Si4

Researchers used a deep-learning composition model to prioritize a sigma-phase ternary compound, synthesized Mo20Re6Si4, and measured bulk superconductivity with a critical temperature of 5.4 K. Magnetic susceptibility and a specific-heat anomaly support the bulk transition. The paper reports mixed model performance on its small test set and describes the model as guidance alongside chemical intuition.

Technology: Deep-learning neural network that classifies compositions as superconducting and predicts critical temperature

  • AI role: Provided composition-based hints that helped researchers select Mo20Re6Si4 for synthesis; laboratory resistivity, magnetic-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements established the superconducting result.

16 Dec 2024Fraunhofer Institute for Algorithms and Scientific Computing (SCAI); University of Bonn; Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School; Boehringer Ingelheim

Deep learning identifies externally replicated fast and slow cognitive-progressor groups in early Alzheimer dementia

Deep learning clustered cognitive and functional trajectories in 283 people with early dementia probably due to Alzheimer disease into fast- and slow-progressing groups. The trajectory groups were externally validated and independently replicated in a 2,779-person dementia cohort. A classifier using cross-sectional data at diagnosis predicted progression group in external validation with AUC 0.70 ± 0.01.

Technology: Deep-learning clustering of longitudinal cognitive/functional trajectories, followed by machine-learning classification from cross-sectional diagnosis data

  • Still unknown: These are prognostic progression groups, not established biological disease subtypes or treatment-response predictors. Trial-size reduction and cost savings were estimated by emulating hypothetical enrichment and were not demonstrated in an actual clinical trial. The study does not show improved patient outcomes.
  • AI role: Deep learning grouped patients using multivariate disease trajectories; the authors then trained a classifier to predict those progression subgroups from measurements available at diagnosis. 15 Dec 2024Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

Active learning identified a KNN ceramic composition with high piezoelectric response

An active-learning loop combined machine-learning prediction, surrogate optimization and experimental testing to explore lead-free potassium-sodium niobate (KNN) ceramics. After three experiment and optimization iterations, the authors report identifying a composition with a measured piezoelectric coefficient d33 of approximately 353 pC/N from thousands of possible compositions. This is a laboratory material-property measurement, not validation of a finished sensor or device.

Technology: Support vector regression with a radial basis function kernel in an active-learning experimental-design loop

13 Dec 2024Onc.AI; Pfizer; University of Pennsylvania; Moffitt Cancer Center

Deep-learning CT response score stratifies outcomes in lung-cancer immunotherapy cohorts

A deep-learning radiomic pipeline generated a pretreatment CT response score (CTRS) for advanced non-small-cell lung cancer treated with PD-(L)1 checkpoint inhibitors. In an independent real-world test cohort, high-response-score first-line ICI-monotherapy patients had longer progression-free and overall survival after adjustment for baseline covariates including PD-L1 (adjusted HR 0.46 and 0.50). In a secondary analysis of 54 participants from a prospective sasanlimab trial, the score was associated with overall survival (adjusted HR 0.33) but not progression-free survival.

Technology: Three-dimensional hierarchical convolutional neural network feature extractor combined with a Cox survival model (CT response score, CTRS)

Relevance 47 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: retrospective or benchmark
  • Tested: In an independent real-world test cohort, high-response-score first-line ICI-monotherapy patients had longer progression-free and overall survival after adjustment for baseline covariates including PD-L1 (adjusted HR 0.46 and 0.50).
  • Still unknown: The real-world data were retrospective. Association of the score with survival among treated patients does not establish that the score predicts differential treatment benefit versus an untreated or alternative-treatment control. Clinical-trial analysis was secondary and small (n=54): PFS association was not significant, while OS association was significant. Authors say larger prospective studies are needed; no improved-care or deployment outcome is shown.
  • AI role: The model learned image features from pretreatment CT/PET-CT scans and combined them with a Cox survival model to produce an imaging-only response score. Researchers evaluated the score in a held-out real-world cohort and in a secondary analysis of a prospective clinical-trial cohort; it stratified PFS/OS in the first and OS in the latter.

12 Dec 2024Forschungszentrum Jülich / Helmholtz Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology; Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology; Xiamen University; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; University of Groningen

Bayesian optimization finds high-performance hole-transport molecules for perovskite solar cells

A closed-loop workflow combined high-throughput synthesis of organic semiconductors, measured photovoltaic-device performance, molecular descriptors and Bayesian optimization to search a virtual library of about one million candidate hole-transport materials. The machine-learning-guided iterations identified high-performing molecules; after device optimization, a perovskite solar cell using a selected material reached 26.23% power-conversion efficiency (25.88% certified). The work links candidate molecular structures to measured device performance in this specific cell system.

Technology: Molecular-descriptor machine-learning models with Bayesian optimization in a high-throughput synthesis and device-testing loop

  • Tested: A closed-loop workflow combined high-throughput synthesis of organic semiconductors, measured photovoltaic-device performance, molecular descriptors and Bayesian optimization to search a virtual library of about one million candidate hole-transport materials.

Bayesian optimization selected new structures from a virtual library of roughly one million; high-throughput synthesis, characterization and device tests supplied feedback for two closed-loop iterations. Three promising molecules then received individual device optimization. This workflow identified hole-transport materials yielding the reported high-efficiency perovskite cells; the AI contribution was candidate selection and structure–performance modeling, with synthesis and measurements performed experimentally.

Evidence sources: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.ads0901

11 Dec 2024Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics; Center for Systems Biology Dresden; TU Dresden Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life

PICNIC machine learning predictions revealed previously poorly characterized human proteins in cellular condensates

The PICNIC gradient-boosting model ranked proteins for membership in biomolecular condensates using sequence-pattern and AlphaFold2-derived structural features. To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold. The experiments mapped examples to cytoplasmic bodies, nuclear bodies, nucleoli or P-bodies; for example, TYW5 and RAD51AP1 showed distinct localization patterns. Across the tested set, the authors found condensate localization was not limited to highly disordered proteins.

Technology: PICNIC, a gradient-boosting machine-learning classifier using protein sequence co-occurrence patterns, sequence complexity/disorder features and AlphaFold2-derived structural features

Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: direct test
  • Tested: To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold.
  • Still unknown: The experimental test used fluorescently tagged proteins expressed in U2OS cells, so observed localization may depend on expression level, tag, cell type or condition. The study did not establish each protein’s endogenous localization or biological function; the authors explicitly state that condensate localization alone makes no functional claim. Three of 24 proteins did not form detectable mesoscale foci, and three additional results were low-confidence under the paper’s size threshold. This is targeted experimental validation of model-selected candidates, not an independently replicated atlas.
  • AI role: PICNIC scored human proteins for likely cellular-condensate membership and selected poorly characterized positive predictions for experimental testing. Its rankings directly guided the 24-protein U2OS localization validation; the model was built to predict condensate members (including clients), not only proteins that self-drive phase separation.

Evidence sources: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-55089-x.pdf

XLuminA computationally discovers a super-resolution microscopy blueprint combining two optical principles

The XLuminA differentiable optical-design system rediscovered established STED beam shaping and optical-vortex approaches, then identified a previously unreported experimental blueprint combining principles from both to produce sub-diffraction imaging in the study’s computational model. This is a specific theoretical/optical-design result, not a report of an independently built and experimentally validated microscope implementing the new blueprint.

9 Dec 2024Northeast Normal University; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Exeter; John Innes Centre; Alan Turing Institute

PlantRNA-FM identifies translation-associated RNA motifs and structure motifs in plants

The PlantRNA-FM model, pretrained on sequence and predicted RNA structure from 1,124 plant transcriptomes, identified 5′-UTR motifs associated with translation efficiency across plant transcriptomes. Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold. The paper reports the rG4 motifs as translation-repressive, consistent with prior evidence on individual rG4s; the transcriptome-wide model prioritization and tested instances are the scoped findings here.

Technology: PlantRNA-FM, an interpretable RNA foundation model integrating RNA sequence and predicted structure

  • Still unknown: Experimental reporter validation was limited to selected motifs and had n=3, as reported in the figure caption. 7 Dec 2024China Geological Survey; Chengdu University of Technology; University of Canterbury; China University of Mining and Technology; Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory; Hunan University of Science and Technology; Nanjing University; China University of Geosciences (Beijing); Chinese Academy of Sciences

Machine-learning classification dates a tectonic transition and probable slab detachment in central Tibet

A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set. Applied to basalts from Tibet’s Bangong–Nujiang suture zone, it found mixed signatures before about 108–107 Ma and only destructive-boundary signatures afterward; the authors interpret the transition as likely oceanic-slab detachment, consistent with other geological evidence.

Technology: Random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element concentrations

Swin-Transformer discovery of planetary nebulae with spectroscopic confirmation in VPHAS+

A Swin-Transformer search of VPHAS+ Hα images identified faint, resolved planetary-nebula candidates in crowded Galactic fields that prior point-source searches missed. Follow-up spectroscopy and HASH classification of 31 targets found 16 true, two likely and four possible planetary nebulae, alongside contaminants and a supernova-remnant fragment. This is one validated search-sample result, not 22 equally secure confirmations.

Representation learning uncovers the extragalactic X-ray transient XRT 200515 in Chandra archives

A representation-learning pipeline searched archived Chandra event data and identified XRT 200515, a previously unnoticed extragalactic fast X-ray transient in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Its light curve has a sharp sub-10-second hard burst followed by an approximately 800-second oscillating tail with spectral softening. The paper discusses possible origins including a low-energy giant magnetar flare or a Type I burst from a faint low-mass X-ray binary; the source's physical nature is unresolved.

Technology: Unsupervised representation-learning pipeline using sparse autoencoders, dimensionality reduction and density-based clustering

20 Nov 2024Sapienza University of Rome; Pennsylvania State University

Deep learning resolves subtle seismic-wave changes across the 2016 Norcia earthquake cycle

A seven-layer convolutional neural network classified raw seismic waveforms recorded near Italy’s 2016 Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake as pre- or post-mainshock and separated time-to-failure intervals with over 90% test accuracy. The authors interpret the model’s performance, frequency dependence and null tests as evidence that local waveforms encode evolving attenuation and elastic properties consistent with progressive fault damage before rupture and postseismic recovery.

Technology: Seven-layer convolutional neural network trained on local seismic waveforms

AI reconstruction extends the 1911 French heatwave signal into September

A partial-convolution U-Net trained on CMIP6 climate simulations and transferred to European station-based extreme indices reconstructed the poorly observed 1911 heatwave. Neural operators reveal nonreciprocal interactions behind microfluidic nonlinear waves

9 Aug 2024University of Cape Town

PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Large Magellanic Cloud pulsars

A MeerKAT survey of its first four Large Magellanic Cloud pointings reported seven new radio pulsars. The search pipeline applied the Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier, to folded candidates and retained candidates above a PICS score threshold before human visual classification. The AI narrowed the candidate set; volunteers performed the final candidate classification and follow-up observations supplied additional checks. Six pulsars were detected again in follow-up; the incoherent-beam pulsar was not. A later paper reports 12 discoveries from additional pointings and timing follow-up of some Paper I pulsars, which are not additional discoveries in this entry.

Technology: Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier for folded candidate plots

Machine-learning-guided proteomics identifies APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 for plaque-rupture classification in acute coronary syndrome

In an acute-coronary-syndrome derivation cohort matched for plaque rupture (PR) versus intact fibrous cap (IFC), quantitative mass spectrometry measured 1,121 plasma proteins. Five machine-learning algorithms screened candidate proteins; APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 were then significantly different between PR and IFC in an independent 85-patient cohort using ELISA. The three proteins discriminated plaque rupture better than the study’s conventional biomarkers and risk factors, suggesting a candidate biomarker panel for identifying PR among ACS patients.

Machine learning identifies plasma protein signatures that predict onset of common and rare diseases

Researchers used regularized machine-learning models to select sparse plasma-protein signatures for 10-year incidence across 218 diseases in 41,931 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants. Five to twenty proteins improved held-out risk prediction over basic clinical information for 67 diseases and over clinical information plus routine assays for 52. The study identified TNFRSF17 as a specific predictor for future multiple myeloma and TNFRSF13B for monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance. In bone-marrow single-cell data from 11 newly diagnosed myeloma patients and three controls, four of five myeloma predictor proteins were most highly expressed by plasma cells; FCRLB and QPCT elevation was attributable to malignant plasma cells. Proteomic signatures also replicated improved prediction for five of six diseases tested in EPIC-Norfolk.

A deep-learning device analyzed routine H&E whole-slide images to estimate whether advanced urothelial tumors carried selected FGFR2/FGFR3 alterations used for erdafitinib eligibility. In a separate 350-slide retrospective validation set, the device achieved 88.7% sensitivity and 31.8% specificity; it was also prospectively integrated into a non-interventional study spanning 89 sites in nine countries. The paper projected a 28.7% reduction in molecular tests assuming 15% biomarker prevalence; that estimate was simulated, not a measured population-level reduction.

Machine-learning analysis linked two sepsis-associated neutrophil clusters to five mouse-validated marker genes

Reanalysis of single-cell profiles from four sepsis patients and two healthy controls identified two neutrophil clusters enriched in the sepsis samples and a set of cluster-associated gene modules. LASSO and seven additional machine-learning classifiers prioritized eight hub genes, including ALPL, CD177, S100A8, S100A9 and STXBP2. Expression analyses in separate public sepsis transcriptome cohorts supported several markers, and qRT-PCR in cecal-ligation/puncture and LPS mouse models found increased neutrophil expression of those five genes. Iterative machine learning identifies potent inhibitors of alpha-synuclein secondary nucleation

A structure-based iterative-learning workflow combined prior α-synuclein fibril-binding hits, a junction-tree variational autoencoder, a random-forest regressor and Gaussian-process residual model to rank compounds for repeated testing. Prospective iterations produced multiple molecules inhibiting seeded α-synuclein aggregation in vitro; lead I4.05 had a reported kinetic inhibitory constant (KIC50) of 0.52 μM (95% CI 0.45–0.59 μM), compared with extrapolated values of 18.2 μM for its parent and 36.4 μM for Anle-138b in the authors’ assay. 11 Apr 2024University of Exeter; Met Office; ETH Zurich; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of Cambridge; University of Leeds; University of Reading

Machine learning reveals tropical aerosol-driven cloud expansion despite stronger rainfall

Using satellite observations of four Kīlauea volcanic outgassing episodes in 2008 and 2018, an ML counterfactual analysis found that volcanic aerosols increased cloud cover and reflected sunlight over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, even as rainfall strengthened. Cloud-cover adjustment contributed about 65% of aerosol–cloud cooling under mixed meteorological conditions and 84–87% in humid conditions; under humid, stable conditions, a 30% increase in droplet number could correspond to up to a 50% relative increase in cloud cover. The result identifies a tropical regime in which aerosol cloud expansion is strong and its response varies with humidity and stability.

Technology: Random-forest machine-learning surrogates of MODIS cloud properties, radiative fluxes, and precipitation, trained on 20 years of satellite observations and meteorology while excluding volcanic years 2008 and 2018

Relevance 53 climate Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

  • Still unknown: This is an observational ML-counterfactual analysis of four Kīlauea plume months over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, not a controlled aerosol intervention or a direct test of deliberate cloud seeding. The source reports strong cloud-cover responses and radiative estimates, especially under humid/stable conditions, but results depend on satellite retrievals and the learned unperturbed baseline. The authors’ proposed mechanism for increased cloud cover alongside stronger rainfall is explicitly a hypothesis requiring further testing; do not treat the marine-cloud-brightening scenario as experimentally demonstrated.
  • AI role: The random-forest surrogates estimated unperturbed cloud properties and radiative fluxes for given meteorological conditions. Comparing those counterfactuals with observations in four volcanic plume episodes isolated aerosol-associated signals from meteorological co-variability and enabled estimates of cloud-cover, rainfall, and radiative-forcing responses across distinct tropical meteorological regimes.

8 Apr 2024The Chinese University of Hong Kong; WSL Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research; Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Sichuan Earthquake Administration; Géoazur

AI-assisted seismic catalog links the 2018 Baige landslide-dammed lakes to increased local earthquakes

An earthquake catalog built with the PhaseNet machine-learning phase detector and cross-correlation/template matching revealed a statistically significant (over 99%) increase in small earthquakes as the second Baige landslide-dammed lake approached peak water level; rates returned toward background after breach. Coulomb-stress modeling found about 90% of the earthquakes in regions of positive modeled stress change, supporting likely triggering through direct water loading and pore-pressure diffusion. The paper presents this as evidence that earthquake–surface-hazard triggering can be bidirectional.

Technology: PhaseNet machine-learning phase detector, combined with PyOcto association and cross-correlation/template-matching methods

Parabacteroides merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine were among the most predictive features; the strain was also the main modeled microbial contributor to the metabolite. In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.

Technology: Tree-based supervised classifiers including random forest, gradient-boosted regression trees, XGBoost, XGBoost-random forest and LightGBM, combined with individualized genome-scale microbiome community models

  • Still unknown: The human data are observational microbiome samples, while intervention was tested in a DSS-induced mouse model, not in people. The model provides candidate prioritization, not a causal human mechanism.
  • AI role: Personalized community metabolic models estimated strain-level contributions to secreted metabolites in human iHMP samples. The AI analysis nominated these targets; it did not establish human therapeutic efficacy.

The scientific result is the disease-specific feature pattern and its validated detection performance, not merely an algorithm benchmark.

  • Still unknown: The 632-object sample comprises 454 unmatched and 178 known objects; unmatched does not mean every object is independently confirmed or has a reliable orbit. Only about 40% of raw objects yielded meaningful distance estimates after filtering. Sizes assume spherical objects and a uniform albedo of 0.15. The authors state that the combined archive sample is not a dedicated or observationally unbiased survey, and the result is an extension of the size-distribution slope to H≈20 rather than a complete census.
  • AI role: The primary study states that the input asteroid trails were detected in the preceding Hubble Asteroid Hunter work using a deep-learning algorithm trained on volunteer classifications. This AI-assisted search supplied the previously unidentified trail sample; the present paper then applies a parallax-fitting method and magnitude-distribution analysis to characterize it. The quantitative population result depends on this archive-scale AI-assisted detection pipeline and the present physical analysis.

Random-forest models trained on UCSF records (749 expert-diagnosed Alzheimer’s disease cases and 250,545 controls) identified clinical features predictive up to seven years before the recorded onset; the seven-year model’s AUROC was 0.72 using clinical features alone. EHR features may reflect healthcare access, clinician behavior, coding and biological processes; the authors explicitly state that further validation across omics data types is needed. Genetic colocalization and matched cohort associations do not establish that osteoporosis causes Alzheimer’s disease or that treating osteoporosis prevents it. The team used matched models to prioritize hypotheses, then used SPOKE to connect clinical predictors to biological networks and independent health-system data plus GWAS/eQTL colocalization to examine the osteoporosis and hyperlipidemia associations. The model-generated prioritization led to follow-up of the female-specific osteoporosis signal near MS4A6A.

Deep learning reveals a new seismicity distribution along the Kabaw Fault in central Myanmar

A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog. The denser catalog shows that shallow Kabaw Fault seismicity disappears south of about 22.8°N while deeper events occur west of the fault, and it fills part of a previously under-sampled seismicity gap; the authors interpret this contrast as potentially reflecting along-strike variation in deformation associated with oblique Indian-plate subduction.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: direct test
  • Tested: The primary article reports successful synthesis of 8 of 13 machine-learning-selected 2D AgBi iodide perovskites (61.5%), with crystal structures determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and bulk-phase purity confirmed by PXRD.
  • Still unknown: The validation concerns a selected set under common laboratory synthesis conditions and one AgBi iodide family; generalization to other material families is not demonstrated.
  • AI role: Subgroup discovery identifies an applicable data region and a support-vector classifier estimates synthesis feasibility from molecular descriptors; the model ranks candidate organic spacers for experimental synthesis.

Evidence sources: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-44236-5.pdf · https://kjc.seu.edu.cn/2024/0111/c29280a478760/page.htm
